title: Self-catheterization of the bladder
also: how to empty the bladder yourself
what: Several times a day you gently insert a thin tube into the urinary channel to let the urine out, and then remove it right away.
why: When the bladder does not empty fully by itself: after spinal injuries, with nerve diseases, after some operations.
duration: one catheterization usually takes 5 to 10 minutes, several times a day
tell_doctor: If it is hard to pass urine or the catheter will not go in
If the urine is cloudy, bloody or smelly
If you are allergic to latex

prepare.title: Training
prepare.text: The first time it is done together with a nurse or urologist. The doctor will say how many times a day.

prepare.title: Catheters
prepare.text: Usually single-use catheters with gel are used. Keep a supply at home and when traveling.

prepare.title: Cleanliness
prepare.text: Wash your hands and the area around the opening before each catheterization.

prepare.title: Fluids
prepare.text: Drink as much as the doctor advises. It affects how often you need the catheter.

bring: A diary: time and amount of urine
A mirror, for women at first
steps: Wash the area around the urinary opening
Open the catheter without touching the tip
Sit on the toilet or stand in front of it, whichever is comfortable
Slowly insert the catheter until urine starts to flow
Wait until the urine stops flowing
Slowly remove the catheter and throw it away
feel: The first times it feels strange and can be unpleasant
There is usually no pain. If it hurts, tell your doctor
after: Catheterize on schedule, even if you do not feel the need to go
Write down the amount of urine if the doctor asked
The catheter is single-use. Do not reuse it
red_flags: Fever, chills, pain in the lower belly or lower back: see a doctor
Blood in the urine that does not clear
You cannot insert the catheter and the bladder is full: see a doctor urgently or call your local emergency number

faq.q: Will regular catheters cause an infection?
faq.a: There is a risk, but clean hands and single-use catheters greatly lower it. Emptying the bladder regularly also protects you.
Yes. Take a supply of catheters and wet wipes with you.

reminders.text: Time for catheterization. Wash your hands and get a new catheter ready.
